speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the mechanism suggests a traumatic injury. Given the 2-day duration of progressive swelling and pain, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or streaking up your arm? REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP; REQUEST IMAGES: X-ray right hand.

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent measurements are normal, which helps rule out systemic infection for now. Based on the mechanism of injury and your symptoms, was there any visible deformity or an inability to extend your finger after the incident? Also, can you describe the specific sensation, such as a "pop" at the time of injury?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to flex your distal interphalangeal joint and the resting extension of the finger strongly suggest a disruption of the extensor mechanism. Can you confirm if you heard a specific "pop" or felt a sharp snap at the moment of injury, and do you see a visible deformity or depression on the top of the finger? DIAGNOSIS READY: Extensor Hallucis Digitorum Mutilans (Ehlers-Danlos) Syndrome is unlikely; the clinical picture of inability to flex, extension lag, and history of trauma is consistent with a Mallet Finger (avulsion fracture or tendon rupture) or a central slip injury (Bonnell-Lhermitte lesion). Given the specific inability to flex the DIP joint, I am confident in the diagnosis of a Mallet Finger.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
